title: Minitel system
summary: France's national videotex network: free dumb terminals (40x25 text, 1200/75 baud) in millions of homes, accessing numbered 3615 services for train times, chat, banking.
mechanism: Numbered-tree service navigation with dedicated function keys (Sommaire/Retour/Envoi/Suite); the whole nation addressable by typing a short code.
decline: Killed by the web's hyperlink model and the metered-billing backlash; network shut down 30 June 2012.
revival_recipe: Rebuild the numbered tree and function-key ritual as a terminal UI layer over local content, minus the metered billing and state monopoly.
levi_application: levi.videotex: browse LEVI's warehouses and docs from any terminal via numbered choices and Minitel keys.
skepticism: Nostalgia glosses over expensive metered billing and the France Telecom monopoly context.

title: Numbered-tree service navigation
summary: Services organized as numbered menus: type a code, confirm, walk down the tree. No hyperlinks, no search box, no mouse.
mechanism: Deterministic addressing - every destination has a short stable code, memorable and speakable, unlike URLs.
decline: Hyperlinks and search won on expressiveness; trees felt constraining once screens could show more.
revival_recipe: Use numbered trees for constrained surfaces: screen readers, serial consoles, low-bandwidth links, where determinism beats expressiveness.
levi_application: Videotex choice chunks (8 per screen, 'suite' for more) give LEVI a UI that works over the dumbest pipe.

title: Minitel function-key ritual
summary: Dedicated keys: Sommaire (contents), Annulation, Retour (back), Repetition (redraw), Guide (help), Correction, Suite (next), Envoi (send/confirm).
mechanism: A fixed, tiny, memorizable command vocabulary shared across every service - learn once, use everywhere.
decline: Died with the hardware; softkeys and gestures replaced fixed function keys.
revival_recipe: Map the ritual onto plain ASCII (*, #, sommaire, suite, guide...) so any terminal speaks it.
levi_application: levi.videotex.keys: one-line parser mapping ASCII to the eight Minitel actions.

title: 3615 metered service codes
summary: Short codes billed per minute (3615 premium and variants); the free terminal was the funnel for metered services.
mechanism: Give away the endpoint, meter the usage - the sly-generosity trade: free hardware as customer acquisition for recurring billing.
decline: Internet flat rates made per-minute billing feel like extortion; the trade moved to app stores and cloud free tiers.
revival_recipe: Study the trade, refuse the billing: LEVI takes the free-endpoint generosity and drops the meter entirely (free forever).
levi_application: The '3615 LEVI' banner is an homage with the meter removed - the generosity without the trap.
skepticism: Do not romanticize: 3615 codes made real money from confused users; the pattern is studied, not revived.

title: Prestel
summary: Britain's videotex system: tree-structured pages of travel, finance, and messaging over phone lines and modified TVs.
mechanism: Same numbered-tree core as Minitel, but on televisions via adapters - meeting users at the screen they already owned.
decline: Expensive sets, thin content, and the web arriving before critical mass.
revival_recipe: Meet users at the terminal they already own: no new hardware, no new app - plain text over stdin/stdout.
levi_application: python -m levi.videotex runs anywhere Python runs, including Termux on a phone.

title: Telidon
summary: Canadian videotex with geometric-primitive graphics instead of block mosaics; technically admired, commercially stillborn.
mechanism: Resolution-independent geometric encoding - describe shapes, not pixels - decades before vector graphics went mainstream.
decline: Better tech, no distribution: without a free-terminal rollout, nobody was on the other end.
revival_recipe: Distribution beats technology: ship on hardware people already have (their existing terminal), not new devices.
levi_application: Videotex ships as pure stdlib Python - zero new dependencies, zero new hardware, runs on what is already there.
skepticism: Telidon's 'superiority' is partly techno-nationalist lore; Minitel won on rollout, not specs.
